prompt: Your team is about to ship an internal authorization middleware that acts as a Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) in front of a set of internal APIs: for every request it builds a policy input from the incoming HTTP request and POSTs it to an external policy engine (a PDP, such as OPA) to get back an allow/deny decision. The author is confident it's safe, reasoning "the policy engine decides everything, so the middleware itself can't be the problem." Please review the middleware below as a security reviewer, not a style reviewer — call out what you consider MUST-FIX authorization bypasses versus what's merely nice-to-have, and explain why.
